description:
Compile Chaprola source (.CS) to bytecode (.PR). READ chaprola://cookbook BEFORE writing source.

AUTO-FIX (default ON): if the source has SQL/JS/Python hallucinations or other compile errors, the platform invokes its system-help expert, takes the corrected source, and recompiles ONCE. If the recompile is clean, the response is a normal success and `auto_fixed.applied` is `true` with the corrections summary + the fixed source. If it's still broken, you get the diagnostics array PLUS `auto_fixed.corrected_source` showing the LLM's best attempt — useful as a starting point for your next rewrite. Pass `systemhelp:"off"` to skip the auto-fix and get raw diagnostics only.

DIAGNOSTICS array: even when auto-fix doesn't apply, every detectable problem in the source comes back in one response — Phase A pre-syntactic guidance (foreign-language keywords, paren math, etc.), Phase B parse errors (up to 25 distinct, with line numbers), and Phase C codegen. No more "fix one error, recompile, see the next" loops.

STYLE RULES (mandatory — project review enforces these):
1. Use QUERY instead of SEEK loops for filtering or single-record lookup. SEEK loops only for processing every record unconditionally.
2. Don't use MOVE + IF EQUAL for comparisons — use QUERY WHERE.
3. Use implicit variable assignment (LET name = value) — don't use DEFINE VARIABLE.
4. END/STOP only for early exit — not needed at end of program.
5. Declare data dependencies in source: OPEN PRIMARY "name" for primary file and OPEN "name" for secondary. The compiler auto-loads format files from these statements; primary_format/secondary_format params are legacy and should not be used for new code.
6. Use named read (READ name rec + name.field) instead of OPEN SECONDARY + S.field for QUERY results.
7. Every program MUST have an intent file (.DS) — one paragraph: what the program does, parameters, output, who uses it.
8. Add a comment header — first lines describe purpose and parameters.
9. Use PRINT concatenation (PRINT "text" + P.field + R1), not MOVE + PRINT 0 buffers.
10. Use RECORDNUMBERS for bulk delete: QUERY INTO name, then DELETE PRIMARY name.RECORDNUMBERS.

KEY SYNTAX: no PROGRAM keyword (start with commands), no commas, LET supports one operation (no parentheses), no built-in functions. P.fieldname and S.fieldname addressing resolve automatically when the source declares OPEN PRIMARY "name" or OPEN "name" for the relevant data file — the compiler loads the format file from those statements. primary_format/secondary_format params exist as a legacy fallback only. If compile fails, call chaprola_help before retrying.

primary_format.description: LEGACY fallback only. Declare the primary file in source with OPEN PRIMARY "name" instead — the compiler auto-loads the format. Do not use for new code.

secondary_format.description: LEGACY fallback only. Declare the secondary file in source with OPEN "name" instead — the compiler auto-loads the format. Do not use for new code.

systemhelp.description: Auto-fix on compile failure. Default 'on' — the platform invokes its system-help expert, takes the corrected source, and recompiles once. Pass 'off' to skip auto-fix and get raw diagnostics only.

userid.description: Project owner's username. Required when accessing a shared project where you are a writer. Defaults to the authenticated user.
